beats.en: Three straight lines that cross each other pairwise can enclose a small region: a triangle. It is the most basic closed shape, and it is strong, which is why bridges and cranes are built from triangles.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 maths · A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: A triangle has three corner points called vertices, and three line segments called sides that join pairs of vertices. The three sides meeting at the corners make three angles.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: A triangle has three corner points called vertices, and three line segments called sides that join pairs of vertices. The three sides meeting at the corners make three angles.
beats.speakEn: A triangle has three corner points called vertices, and three line segments called sides that join pairs of vertices. The three sides meeting at the corners make three angles.

beats.en: An equilateral triangle has all its sides equal. It is the most symmetric of all triangles. To draw one with sides 4 cm, first draw the base AB of 4 cm.
beats.speakEn: An equilateral triangle has all its sides equal. It is the most symmetric of all triangles. To draw one with sides 4 centimetres, first draw the base AB of 4 centimetres.

textbookBox.concept: To construct a triangle with sides 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm, choose one side as the base, say 4 cm, and call its ends A and B. The point C is 5 cm from A, so it lies on a circle of radius 5 cm around A.

beats.en: To construct a triangle with sides 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm, choose one side as the base, say 4 cm, and call its ends A and B. The point C is 5 cm from A, so it lies on a circle of radius 5 cm around A.

beats.en: Try to construct a triangle with sides 3 cm, 4 cm and 8 cm. The two arcs never meet. Try 2 cm, 3 cm and 6 cm. Again it fails. So some sets of lengths make a triangle and others do not.
beats.speakEn: Try to construct a triangle with sides 3 centimetres, 4 centimetres and 8 centimetres. The two arcs never meet. Try 2 centimetres, 3 centimetres and 6 centimetres. Again it fails. So some sets of lengths make a triangle and others do not.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 7 maths · A Tale of Three Intersecting Lines · Complete Summary
textbookBox.concept: For a triangle to exist, each side must be less than the sum of the other two sides. This is called the triangle inequality. It is enough to compare the longest side with the sum of the other two.
